learning_objective: 🎯 Take the action to the big fields! Learn the rules, formations, and skills of outdoor team sports like Football, Hockey, and Cricket.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Played with 11 players per team. The goal is to score by putting the ball in the opponent's net using any body part except hands and arms. Requires immense cardiovascular endurance.
An attacking player cannot be closer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender when the ball is passed to them. It prevents 'cherry-picking' near the goal.
Also played with 11 players. Players use a J-shaped stick to dribble, pass, and shoot a hard ball. Important rules include using only the flat side of the stick and the 'Penalty Corner'.
A bat-and-ball game played between two teams of 11. It involves batting, bowling, and fielding. Formats include Test matches, ODIs, and T20s. Requires high hand-eye coordination.
Field sports rely heavily on formations (like 4-4-2 in football) to control the large space. Coaches act like chess masters, assigning specific attacking and defensive roles to players.

fun_activity.title: ♟️ Be the Coach
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a football field on a piece of paper. Use coins or buttons to create a 4-3-3 formation (4 defenders, 3 midfielders, 3 forwards, 1 goalie). See how spacing works on the field!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the duration of standard matches: Football (90 mins), Hockey (60 mins in four quarters).
📌 Be able to explain the Offside rule in football simply.
📌 In hockey, remember that the ball cannot intentionally touch a player's feet (foul).
quick_recap: ⭐ The goalkeeper is the only player in football allowed to use their hands (inside the penalty box).
⭐ A cricket pitch is exactly 22 yards long.
⭐ Field sports require high levels of stamina because players cover large distances over a long period.
